submissions.title: Data center moratorium takes first steps after Fort Worth City Council's unanimous vote
submissions.excerpt: Fort Worth City Council voted unanimously to begin the legal process for a proposed 90-day moratorium on new data center development.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Fort Worth City Council voted unanimously on Aug 11, 2026 to begin the legal process toward a 90-day moratorium on new data center construction. This is only the first procedural step — if ultimately adopted, the moratorium would take effect Feb 16, 2027 after required public hearings and a report from the city's Data Center & Infrastructure Committee; zoning applications filed before then stay outside it. Draft staff rules would also bar cryptocurrency mining data centers and confine the use to industrially zoned land. Not tied to any single tracked project — a general municipal policy; no projectId. submissions.note: Tracked project: TeraWulf Lake Mariner (slug terawulf-lake-mariner-fluidstack-anthropic), status UNDER_CONSTRUCTION, currently tracked confirmedMw=360. submissions.title: No. 62: Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers in New York While the State Develops Higher Standards for Data Center Development and Benefits Blueprint to Support Localities
submissions.publisher: Office of Governor Kathy Hochul, New York State
submissions.excerpt: Immediately pausing discretionary state environmental permits for any data center capable of using 50 megawatts of electricity or more.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Gov. Hochul's Executive Order 62 (signed July 14, 2026) immediately paused new NYS DEC discretionary environmental permits for data centers able to use 50 MW or more, pending a Generic Environmental Impact Statement Hochul says will take roughly a year; exempts manufacturing/medical/education/research facilities and any DEC application already deemed complete before July 14. Described as the first statewide data center permitting moratorium in the US.
